stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 10, Topic 8.4, The Interstate Highway Act and Suburban Growth and the Rise of the Sunbelt.
stimulus.text: The National Interstate and Defense Highways Act of 1956 launched a massive federal highway-building project. The highways were promoted as a defense measure, to move troops and military equipment quickly, and they let drivers travel fast from suburbs into cities. At the same time, Americans moved in large numbers to the Sunbelt states of the South and West, drawn by jobs, warm weather, and new industries. By 1956, a majority of American workers held white-collar jobs.

stem: By 1956, a majority of American workers held white-collar jobs. That fact best supports which claim about the postwar economy?

options.text: Factory and farm work had vanished from the United States
options.misconception: Background from the books: factories still made cars and appliances and farms still grew food; office work grew beside them, it did not erase them.

options.text: Most Americans had stopped working for wages entirely
options.misconception: Background from the books: white-collar workers are wage workers in offices; the fact says their kind of job changed, not that work ended.

options.text: The economy was shifting from factory and farm work to offices
The government had banned blue-collar jobs by law
options.misconception: Background from the books: no law banned blue-collar jobs; the shift came from growth in offices and services.

rationales.A: Background from the books: factories still made cars and appliances and farms still grew food; office work grew beside them, it did not erase them.
rationales.B: Background from the books: white-collar workers are wage workers in offices; the fact says their kind of job changed, not that work ended.
rationales.C: A majority in offices means office work had passed factory and farm work as the main kind of job, which is a shift in the economy's shape.
rationales.D: Background from the books: no law banned blue-collar jobs; the shift came from growth in offices and services.
rationales.general:
1. A majority is a tipping point: more than half of workers now held office jobs.
2. Background from the books: the postwar economy grew through services, offices, and new industries as well as factories.
3. When the majority kind of job changes, the economy itself has changed shape.
Remember: A majority in a table marks a turning point, not just a big number.
